correctness.rationale: Ultrahomogeneity identifies each nonalgebraic extension with one downset L, one upset U and all l<u cross-pairs. One-sided patterns contribute 2J-1. For mixed patterns, common upper neighbors are counted for singleton lower subset (7n choices), adjacent pair (3n), distance-two pair (n), and cyclic triple (n), with no other common upper neighbors for n>=5. Thus M=12n. An ideal is encoded by choice of upper vertices, with each lower not forced by a selected top vertex providing weight 2: J=sum_{z in {0,1}^n} 2^{#cyclic zero triples}. A four-state weighted transition T has characteristic polynomial z(z-1)(z²-2z-1), yielding J=1+(1+sqrt2)^n+(1-sqrt2)^n. Independent subset enumeration for n=5..11 confirmed t=225,469,1041,2405,5681 for first five n and M=12n; complete all-n proof is transfer-matrix and incidence argument.

Adding 2n algebraic types gives all 1-types. Mixed proportion decays exponentially.
